posts.author: Sergio
posts.content_md:
Recently Polygrama developed a dry photopolymer film (name CROMA) intended for a versatile high efficient photopolymer. Exposed with a good beam ratio for a reflection hologram, after UV curing it can be used with the same wavelength reply as a master, but after removing the special film cover the hologram is air developed to a level (depending on beam ratio quality) of a "DCG" appearance with a marked bandwidth increase.

The result polymer is stable to environment and scratch resistant.

Green (532nm) and Red (635nm) sensitive.

Small samples are available and the possible use substituting the embossed hologram marketing is real with lower cost.

Regards,

Sergio Oliveira.

posts.author: Sergio
posts.content_md:
Hans, we usually work with gratings and they are somewhat tricky to photograph, I'm forwarding some material to Martin holograph in H2 mode but [here](http://www.mediafire.com/imageview.php?quickkey=awdy3bzpnqz&thumb=4) is a pic of the Czech team:

![Image](http://www.mediafire.com/imgbnc.php/73e52ee6044c42291b0c977b4bb17fdf4g.jpg)

This is a full set of interferograms made with our Base polymer SM-532TR that is used with Croma, they are low noise. The intensity of the reference and the object waves was equal and was set at 100 uW/cm2. To reach the exposure of 12 mJ/cm2 were required approximately 60 seconds, representing different modes of piezoelectric unimorph vibrations of various sizes influenced by the position of the holder.

Photo by Technical University of Liberec.

Sergio.

So, Let me see if i've got this correct...

> To reach the exposure of 12 mJ/cm2

So, assuming an exposure energy required for the plate of 12uJ cm^2

Using my 532nm C315m at 100mW (100000uJ of energy), I expand the beam to 25.40 cm (area of 506.77 cm^2) and expose a 12cm x 10cm plate ( area of 120cm^2).

The expanded beam contains an energy of 197.33uJ cm^2

The total energy hitting the plate is 23679.23uJ

This gives a theoretical exposure time of 0.06 of a second.

That's fast !!, is that correct, anyone care to check the calculation???

Jem

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
You made a small mistake Jem.

The power of the expanded beam is 197uW/cm^2. That means that the energy per square cm hitting the plate is 197.33uJ per second. (Assuming no Gaussian profile). The material needs 12 mili Joule per cm^2. So the exposure time would be around 12000/197 = 61 seconds.
